Intro.title: About
Intro.lead: I'm a Senior Frontend Engineer with 5 years of experience, currently leading frontend at Datasport Germany. I like to keep things short and to the point — so I'll do the same here.
Intro.drive: What drives me: I like understanding systems end-to-end — not just building what's specified, but digging into requirements with product owners and designers until the details are actually clear.
Intro.scale: I care about building things that scale beyond one feature — design systems, reusable components, code that other engineers can build on without guessing.
Intro.mentoring: I also enjoy mentoring — code review, pairing, helping engineers grow into independent contributors.
Intro.communication: And I value direct communication — I'd rather flag a problem early than let it surface late. Keeps the whole team moving.

uni-donate.title: uni-donate

orbit.title: Orbit

omm.title: Omm

ai-tooling-security.title: AI Tooling Security
ai-tooling-security.description: Investigating AI-agent tooling and where the holes are — threat-modelling what happens when a compromised agent reaches docker.sock, and prototyping a proxy layer that filters agent output.

sporTechCompany.summary: Sports-event SaaS for 500K+ participants — CRM, registration, payments, an embeddable B2B widget, and athlete accounts.
bullets: Led frontend architecture for a participant-management CRM and registration platform, rebuilding it after a prior vendor engagement and restructuring delivery for a leaner cost base while retaining all key clients.
Rebuilt the core participant form (40K+ LOC, 40+ interdependent fields, DSL-driven conditional logic) plus a virtualized grid handling thousands of rows.
Shipped a public multi-step registration wizard with SEPA/PayPal/Payrexx payments, supporting high-profile client launches.
Built an embeddable, themeable registration widget (web components + MUI CSS-in-JS) that enabled a new B2B integration.
Designed corporate group registration for large-scale events (500K+ participants).
Built a private, test-covered React/TypeScript UI kit reused across multiple internal products.

Built an AI coaching product end-to-end, solo at the start — Next.js/PWA frontend, NestJS backend, and integration with a Python-based AI service, reviewing its contracts directly to wire them into the frontend. A backend engineer later joined to help scale delivery.

addTechCompany.role: Senior Frontend Developer / Senior React Developer
addTechCompany.summary: Media-planning SaaS: micro-frontends, a virtualized reference grid, and drag-and-drop workflows.
bullets: Owned micro-frontends on a media-planning platform with CI/CD (Jenkins, Bitbucket); took part in cross-team code reviews and TDD.
Rebuilt the platform's media-plan data table (column resizing, drag-and-drop), which became the reference implementation across the platform.
Contributed to launching a second product and piloted new engineering practices for the team.

BeyondCode.title: The part that explains the rest.

music.title: Music, 15 years
music.body: Recorder from age four — learned notes before letters — and trumpet from 11 to 19. Handel, Albinoni, Piazzolla; originals only. Music taught me precision: small details compound into masterpieces, or into bugs.

boxing.title: Boxing
boxing.body: A year and a half of it. Discipline, and staying calm when hit.

books.title: Books
books.body: Tom Sawyer, the Orthodox Bible, and on the reread list: Goethe's Faust, Dante, Gorky's Danko — the man who carried everything alone. Carrying everything solo was my biggest flaw; delegation is the fix.

pattern-matching.title: Pattern-matching
pattern-matching.body: Attentive by nature — I remember key facts and build cause-and-effect chains like a detective. It found the vulnerabilities; it also gets me called paranoid. Both are true costs of the same skill.
